subject: EdgeWell on-prem K8s — storage, networking, and airgap acceptance
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@edgewell.com>

Subject: Private cluster preflight — storage/encryption/egress questions

Hi Marissa / team,

Thanks again for the preflight template — I attached a filled draft (edgewell-preflight-checklist.xlsx). We're starting the internal review with our infrastructure and security teams and have a few clarifying questions before the workshop: 

- Airgapped constraints: we need to confirm what outbound egress Redwood requires for health checks, model updates, and telemetry. Can those be allowed via a proxy with allowlistable IPs?
- Persistent volumes: we'd like to use host-attached NVMe for ephemeral caches and a local blockstore for model weights. Do you recommend separating the PVC classes (ephemeral-local vs. backed-blockstore) and how does Redwood handle cache eviction when node drains occur?
- Encryption in transit and at rest: we need a short statement of Redwood's recommended configuration for KMS/HSM usage on private deployments (we use HashiCorp Vault internally).
- Time sync / NTP and OS patching: our compliance team wants a minimal acceptable SLO for time drift and a recommended cadence for security updates before handover.

We also dropped in a high-level network diagram request (see network-drawings.pdf) — would appreciate a short list of required VLANs, firewall rules, and any ports that must be opened for the control plane and agent communication.

Proposed slot for the workshop: Tue Aug 3 or Wed Aug 4 (US/PST). Happy to move if you prefer another date.

Attachments: edgewell-preflight-checklist.xlsx

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Private cluster preflight — storage/encryption/egress questions

Hi Daniel — great to see the filled checklist, and thanks for the diagram. Quick answers and next steps below; we should reserve 60–90 minutes for the workshop to walk drawings and runbook.

Short answers:
- Egress: Private deployments can be configured behind a customer-managed proxy (outbound only). We support a small set of allowlist IPs for model pulls, health probes, and heartbeat telemetry. If you want zero external outbound, we can discuss a manual model provisioning flow during the workshop.
- PVCs and tiers: yes — we strongly recommend two storage classes: 
  * ephemeral-local (local NVMe, ReclaimPolicy=Delete, medium QoS) for KV caches and scratch;
  * durable-block (iSCSI/NAS or customer blockstore, ReclaimPolicy=Retain, high QoS) for model weights and stateful components.
  On node drains Redwood's runtime will attempt graceful KV flush to durable-block where configured; otherwise cached data is best-effort. We'll document recommended cache sizes and eviction triggers in the runbook.
- Encryption/KMS: we integrate with customer Vault/HSM via a KMS shim for key wrapping. Best practice: customer-controlled keys for model-at-rest encryption + mTLS between pods and the control plane. We'll provide a short integration checklist for Vault in the workshop.
- Time sync / patching: acceptable time drift < 500ms for certificate validation. Recommended patch cadence: monthly security patching with a staged canary on non-prod nodes and a quarterly full patch window for private clusters.

Action items for the workshop:
1) Network rule set (we'll bring a poster of required ports and default VLANs).
2) Storage class mapping to node pools and an eviction/restore play for KV caches.
3) KMS integration checklist and a sample policy for Vault.
4) Outbound egress options (proxy vs manual model load).

Proposed attendees from Redwood: myself (technical PM), Laura Bennett (deployment lead), Karthik Iyer (infrastructure architect), Stephanie Nguyen (security lead).

Confirming Tue Aug 3, 10:00–11:30 PST works for us — I'll send a calendar invite with the preliminary agenda and link to the Drive folder.

Attachments: redwood-private-deploy-notes.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Private cluster preflight — storage/encryption/egress questions

Daniel / team — quick technical notes to add to Marissa's summary: 

- Node classes / taints:
  * control-plane (3x control VMs, tainted, no workloads)
  * workload-gpu (GPU instances, local NVMe for checkpointing)
  * workload-ssd (fast blockstore; model weights live here)
  * burst-cpu (spot-like, for batch jobs; tolerant of eviction)

- Storage specifics:
  * KV cache recommendations: allocate 20–25% of node NVMe to avoid OOM. Use LVM thin if you need dynamic allocation.
  * For model weight durability we recommend multipath block devices to your NAS (or blockstore) and the durable-block storage class with ReadWriteOnce + snapshot schedule (daily for prod).
  * If you cannot provide a network-attached blockstore, we can stage model weights on an init container that pulls compressed blobs from an offline media during maintenance windows.

- Drains & eviction handling: plan for pre-drain sync hooks that flush the runtime KV to durable-block. We can ship a small operator to coordinate that as part of the private package.

- Ports: control-plane: 6443 (kube API), 10250 (kubelet), 2379 (etcd) — agent heartbeats are over 443/mTLS. We'll produce a minimal iptables/ACL list.

I'll drop a short note on expected IOPS for model-weight reads in the Drive folder before the workshop.
